speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in today. You mentioned a history of gait and limb ataxia; to help me understand the underlying cause, could you please describe when these symptoms first started and how they have progressed over time?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description. Since you are experiencing clumsiness specifically on the right side, have you noticed any weakness, numbness, or difficulty speaking on that side as well?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a crucial piece of information. Given your history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab, have you noticed any visual disturbances like double vision or loss of vision in one eye, or any recent infections like the flu?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Natalizumab-associated Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML).

REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with and without contrast.
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Brain_Axial_Sagittal.
